new_features.name: Recover from an application error
new_features.description: Recover from an application render or startup-module failure by reloading Suite or clearing its local database and reloading.
new_features.platform_notes: Desktop/web show the shared generic Error component after an exception reaches Main’s error boundary; Electron module-load failure can also render it. Native composition does not establish an equivalent generic render-error recovery screen; its separately mapped MMKV storage-recovery alert must not be treated as this feature.

navigation.desktop: Automatic error fallback after an application render or startup-module failure > Reload window / Clear storage and reload
navigation.web: Automatic error fallback after an application render failure > Reload window / Clear storage and reload

evidence.detail: Generic fallback displays an error heading/message, Reload window (reloadApp), and Clear storage and reload (db.removeDatabase followed by reloadApp).
React error boundary sends error.message to the generic Error component; the triggering exception need not be a database-loading failure.
Shared desktop/web composition wraps router and application content in the generic boundary.
Electron startup also renders the shared ErrorScreen when native-module loading fails.
Startup ErrorScreen composes the same Error component in a theme provider.
Database corruption instead routes to DatabaseCorruptedModal, establishing a different trigger and user-facing recovery surface.
Database-specific recovery presents its own critical dialog and resetSuiteAppThunk action; it is already mapped as database-recovery.
Native root uses its own provider/navigation composition; the shared desktop/web Error component is not composed here.
Native app wrapping provides no inspected custom generic recovery UI matching these two controls; native parity remains unknown.
Native Restart app/Clear app storage alert handles MMKV initialization failure and belongs to existing database-recovery, not proof of generic render-error recovery.
Adjacent ordinary Settings reset scenario supplies only weak ownership/domain evidence; it does not test the generic Error screen.

ownership.basis: Weak product-team estimate inherited from the Application maintenance domain and its reset manual TestStream.Growth; no accountable owner is explicitly declared for the generic fallback, and CODEOWNERS does not establish product ownership.

conditions: An error must reach the shared React error boundary, or Electron startup module loading must fail; ordinary error-free navigation does not display this screen.
The generic fallback may replace the current feature during rendering; it is not entered through the normal Settings reset control.

Reload window invokes reloadApp without deleting the database. Clear storage and reload invokes db.removeDatabase and then reloadApp; the component does not await deletion or use the comprehensive Settings reset thunk.
Native generic fallback parity is unknown after inspecting its root composition and storage recovery; the known MMKV-specific recovery remains mapped separately.
The original exception text can contain diagnostic input; capture only the authorized safe QA failure context and do not transcribe account/device values into map metadata.

screenshot.notes: This source proposal makes no capture claim. The root runtime audit will attach its actually reached QA error-screen capture separately.

notes: Distinct user-facing outcome: existing database-recovery covers explicit IndexedDB/MMKV initialization failures; this generic render/module-load fallback handles a different trigger and offers a non-destructive reload alternative alongside local-database deletion.
Existing app-settings.reset covers an ordinary Settings maintenance workflow and broader resetSuiteAppThunk behavior. Generic Error directly calls db.removeDatabase and reloadApp instead.

No dedicated automated or manual scenario asserting the generic Error screen/buttons was found in inspected Suite and native E2E/test sources. The adjacent manual Settings reset test is labeled only as ownership/domain evidence, not functional coverage.

Source-derived proposal only. The root audit reported an actually reached QA error state, but this agent did not execute the app, verify recovery actions, edit the main manifest or invent a runtime observation.
Parent IDs and related IDs intentionally reference existing canonical features for this additive extension.
